cues.text: A stone house on the mountain
Luka Modrić was born in 1985 near Zadar, in Croatia.
He spent most of his early years in a stone house on the slopes of the Velebit mountain, where his grandfather lived.
Luka was named after him.
At five, he helped look after the goats.
In 1991 a war came to the area, and the family had to leave their home.
That December, his grandfather Luka was killed near the house, and later the house was burned down.
Lift the photo frame to remember him.
When you lose someone you love, it’s okay to feel sad. Share your memories with people you trust.
A hotel for a home
Luka and his family became refugees.
For seven years they lived in the Hotel Kolovare in Zadar, and later in the Hotel Iž.
His father joined the Croatian Army and worked on aircraft.
In those years, many bombs fell on the city.
Roll the ball across the car park.
Luka mostly played football in the hotel’s parking lot, and football was a way to escape the war.
He later said he made friends with many other children, and their parents did not let the war spoil their childhood.
In hard times, friends and play can help. It’s okay to have fun even when life is difficult.
The people behind him
In 1992, Luka started primary school and joined a sports academy too.
His family had very little money, but they paid for the academy, and sometimes his uncle helped.
Supported by his family, he trained at the club NK Zadar.
Lift the three flaps to see who helped.
There was his family, his uncle, and Tomislav Bašić, the head of the youth academy, whom Luka calls his sporting father.
When people believe in you, you don’t have to carry everything alone.
You don’t have to face hard things alone. Family, friends and coaches can be your team.
Too small, they said
The big club Hajduk Split did not sign Luka, because they thought he was too young and too light.
Many young players would feel like giving up.
Luka kept playing.
Open the gate.
His coach, Tomislav Bašić, helped him move to Dinamo Zagreb at sixteen.
In 2003 Dinamo loaned him to Zrinjski Mostar in Bosnia, a very tough league, and at eighteen he was its Player of the Year.
In 2005, with his first long contract, he bought a flat in Zadar for his family.
Being small, or hearing no, is not the end. Keep going, and another door can open.
Called a lightweight
In 2008 Luka moved to Tottenham Hotspur in England.
At first it was hard.
He hurt his knee, and some newspapers, and even Arsenal’s manager, called him a lightweight.
Luka later said critics push you forward to show them they are wrong.
In 2009 he broke a bone in his right leg and was out until December.
Unfold the bridge back to the pitch.
When he returned, he scored in his first game back, using the leg he had broken.
What other people say doesn’t decide who you are. You can come back from a setback.
Welcome home
At the 2018 World Cup, Croatia played Denmark.
Luka took a penalty in extra time, and the goalkeeper saved it.
But in the shoot-out he stepped up again and scored, and Croatia went through.
They reached their first World Cup final, and lost 4–2 to France.
Luka was still named the best player of the tournament, and later won the Ballon d’Or.
Raise the welcome banner.
Back in Zadar, where he had lived as a refugee, tens of thousands of people welcomed him home.
A miss is not the end. Be brave enough to try again, and remember where you came from.
